title: APS: Adaptive Partitioning-Based Frame Selection for Long Video Understanding
abstract: arXiv:2611.24079v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Recent advances in large vision-language models (LVLMs) have significantly improved video understanding capabilities, yet processing long videos remains challenging due to the substantial computational cost of extensive visual inputs. Frame selection offers an efficient alternative, but many existing region-based methods rely on fixed or predefined temporal partitions, which may result in suboptimal temporal regions, compromising subsequent budget allocation and frame selection. In this work, we propose Adaptive Partitioning-Based Frame Selection (APS), a training-free framework that adapts temporal partitions to local variations in query-frame relevance. Specifically, APS formulates temporal partitioning as a complexity-regularized fitting problem, jointly optimizing partition boundaries and local models through dynamic programming. translated_title: APS：基于自适应分区的长视频理解帧选择方法
translated_abstract: 大型视觉语言模型（LVLM）的最新进展显著提升了视频理解能力，然而由于海量视觉输入带来的高昂计算成本，长视频处理仍然充满挑战。帧选择提供了一种高效的替代方案，但许多现有的基于区域的方法依赖于固定或预定义的时间分区，这可能导致所选时间区域次优，从而影响后续的预算分配与帧选择。在本工作中，我们提出了基于自适应分区的帧选择方法（APS），这是一个无需训练的框架，能够根据查询-帧相关性的局部变化自适应地调整时间分区。具体而言，APS将时间分区问题形式化为一个带复杂度正则化的拟合问题，通过动态规划联合优化分区边界和局部模型。由此得到的自适应时间分区能够根据查询相关性以及时间……
tldr: 提出了一种无需训练的自适应分区帧选择框架APS，将时间分区形式化为复杂度正则化的拟合问题并通过动态规划联合优化分区边界与局部模型，从而依据查询-帧相关性高效分配帧预算，提升长视频理解性能。
en_tdlr: APS is a training-free frame selection framework that adaptively partitions the temporal dimension by formulating partitioning as a complexity-regularized fitting problem solved via dynamic programming, enabling query-relevance-based frame budget allocation for improved long video understanding.
